assessment_summary: Validation approach: (1) Confirmed installation context — repo at /workspace at commit d9bf927 (matches summary), manual Docker Compose deployment from /workspace/deploy/compose/example/local using -f ../../docker-compose.yaml --env-file .env, as described. (2) Verified prerequisites (Docker 29.7.2, Compose v5.5.0). (3) Verified runtime state via docker ps and docker compose ps: all 9 documented containers (core, portal, jobservice, registryctl, registry, trivy-adapter, exporter, postgres, redis/valkey) running healthy with the documented v2.15.0 remote images, correct port mappings (80/443 on host), and named volumes. (4) Verified the guide's functional claims: UI at http://localhost returns HTTP 200 with Harbor HTML; /api/v2.0/health reports all 8 components healthy; admin/Harbor12345 login yields a working JWT and authenticated API access (projects list returns the default 'library' project); the guide's exact login command `docker login localhost:80 -u admin --password-stdin` succeeds; a full push (tag alpine → localhost:80/library/alpine:validation-test) and pull round-trip succeeded, and the pushed tag/artifact is visible through both the registry v2 API and the Harbor artifacts API, confirming registry push/pull functionality end-to-end. (5) Verified setup artifacts: .env (only intended diff from .env.example: IMAGE_REPO set) and the 4096-bit RSA token_service_key.pem (mode 644, `openssl rsa -check` → 'RSA key ok'). Core logs confirm Harbor 2.15.0, successful DB migration, and Trivy scanner registration.\n\nLimitations: I could not verify the browser-based login UI interactively, but the login is proven via the token endpoint used by that UI. The optional mkcert HTTPS section was not performed, consistent with the TLS-disabled local configuration the guide presents as the default and the installer's stated intent — not a failure. One minor unresolved item: the extra tag 'validation-test' I created during validation could not be deleted via the Harbor API (DELETE /projects/library/repositories/alpine/artifacts/{digest}/tags/validation-test returned 401 even with a correctly delete-scoped token from http://localhost/service/token, and 405 for GET) — an apparent token/RBAC quirk of this deployment fork, not an installation defect; it does not affect any guide-documented behavior (push/pull/UI/health all work) and the tag references the same artifact digest as the installer's pre-existing 'test' tag, so it adds no new data. I also could not remove the validation image tag from the local docker cache without deleting the installer's tag (same digest). None of these affect the completeness or operability of the installation as documented in the guide.
